content:
The test image shows:
- Affected part: stem and leaves
- One side of the plant has completely wilted, desiccated, brown/dark leaves hanging dead
- The stem shows clear dark brown/reddish-brown discoloration
- Neighboring leaves on the other side remain green and healthy
- Some whitish material visible at the node junction
- Asymmetric, one-sided wilting pattern

This strongly suggests a vascular/stem disease. Top candidates: Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (desiccation of leaves + stem canker), Verticillium_Wilt (one-sided wilting + vascular discoloration), or Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (dark stem lesions).

Now I'll view one reference image to confirm — checking Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato stem since the desiccated leaves and stem canker pattern match most closely.

The reference image shows Bacterial Canker — an internal cross-section with brown vascular rot and surrounding desiccated leaves.

Comparing to the test image:
- Test image shows a lateral stem/petiole with dark reddish-brown discoloration throughout its length
- Leaves on that dark stem are completely desiccated and dead (brown, shriveled, hanging)
- The main stem remains green; healthy leaves on the other side
- A lesion is visible at the node junction with some whitish material

This matches Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato very well: "wilting, defoliation, and desiccation of leaves, along with brown canker lesions on stems" and "excessive wilting, canker development." The complete one-sided desiccation of an entire branch is characteristic. The dark stem discoloration represents the external canker spreading along the lateral stem.
